_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), whatpub.com and Altrincham Today: Prana, 14-16 Ashley Road, Altrincham WA14 2DW, an independent live-music venue and cocktail bar opened November 2023, run by the same team as Amp in Stockport — a real 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, same precedent as Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme's Mounting Stone/Chiverton Tap pair in this batch. RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-11 (curia-suggestion-review) found the original researcher's 'CAMRA-listed and actively promoted' claim was incomplete: CAMRA and whatpub.com both actually list Prana as 'Closed Long Term' (last updated 28/05/2024), following a reported 'closing until further notice' Facebook announcement from Altrincham Today around the same date — a real closure signal the original pass missed. However, a new company, PRANA F&B LIMITED, was incorporated 13 September 2024 at the same 14-16 Ashley Road address and remains active per Companies House, and a Food Hygiene Ratings record exists for 'Prana - Altrincham' — both consistent with a reopening or change of hands rather than the site sitting empty, but no direct evidence of current 2025/2026 trading (a recent event listing, an active social post) was found either way. Genuinely conflicting signals rather than a clean pass or fail — left pending here and sent to docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than promoted or rejected outright.

suggestions.name: Residence Restaurant & Bar
suggestions.reason: A Georgian mansion just off the square, quietly renovated twice in seventeen years without losing the panelled bar — order the wood-fired pizza in the courtyard and let the high street disappear.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Dawnvale's own project case study (dawnvale.com), Yelp and OpenTable: Residence Restaurant & Bar, 9 Mill Street, Nantwich CW5 5ST, opened 2007 in a Grade-II Georgian mansion, refitted 2017 with a courtyard extension and wood-fired pizza oven — single-site, no other locations found anywhere. Confirmed currently trading (live OpenTable bookings, recent reviews). Real gluten-free menu confirmed (findmeglutenfree.com); no vegan/dog-friendly confirmation found, left at safe default. Coordinates are an approximate Mill Street position cross-checked against multiple independent citations for nearby Mill Street addresses — api.postcodes.io and doogal.co.uk (this file's usual per-postcode geocoding sources) were both blocked by this session's network egress policy, so this is a slightly rougher fix than the file's usual precision; flagged for the reviewer to tighten if possible. Reuses the existing BISTRO type (Chestergate Bistro, Macclesfield) rather than introducing a new one. Fills part of Nantwich's real gap — the district had zero venues before this run, the most acute gap of any district in the roster today (re-tallied against the live venues.json this run: nantwich 0, macclesfield 3, bramhall 5, heaton-moor 6, stockport-underbanks 7, prestbury 8, then a cluster of 9s).

suggestions.name: Black Lion
suggestions.reason: Nantwich's oldest pub by two centuries, free enough of any brewery's say-so to swap the pumps on a whim — a former Dorchester chef runs the kitchen now, and the goat curry has no business being this good in a 1664 taproom.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the pub's own site (blacklionnantwich.co.uk/history) and The Nantwich News (named in the Telegraph's 2026 Top UK Pubs Guide): Black Lion, 29 Welsh Row, Nantwich CW5 5ED — a genuine freehouse, no brewery or pub-company tie of any kind, run by Darren and business partner Louise Gulland since just before Covid; listed in CAMRA's Good Beer Guide every year since digital records began. The opposite case from the Robinsons/Hydes tied houses already excluded elsewhere in this file. Real dog-friendly (downstairs only) and vegan-adaptable (Vn-marked menu items) confirmations both found via the venue's own menu page. Coordinates approximate Welsh Row's known building positions (egress to postcodes.io/doogal.co.uk blocked this run, see Residence Restaurant & Bar's note above for the same caveat).

suggestions.name: Deadwood Smokehouse
suggestions.reason: American barbecue smoked in-house on Beam Street rather than trucked in from somewhere else — book ahead, because the brisket runs out most nights before nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (deadwoodsmokehouse.com), Tripadvisor (4.2/5, ranked among Nantwich's top restaurants) and CAMRA: Deadwood Smokehouse, 16 Beam Street, Nantwich CW5 5LL. A real 2-site sibling pair with a second Deadwood in Mold, North Wales — the same single-sibling-location precedent already established for Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields/Fire Station Social Cucina, not a chain footprint. Dog-friendly explicitly confirmed for the outdoor frontage seating only (not inside) — marked petFriendly true on that real, if partial, confirmation. No vegan/gluten-free menu explicitly confirmed despite a direct search; left at safe default. Introduces a new type, SMOKEHOUSE — no existing Eat type fits a dedicated American BBQ smokehouse; left category-only (Eat) in tile-catalog-map.ts, same precedent as CANTONESE ROAST/GREEK TAVERNA. Coordinates approximate Beam Street's known building positions (geocoding API access blocked this run, see above).

suggestions.name: The Nest Nantwich
suggestions.reason: A working still behind the bar on Pepper Street — order the tasting flight before the cocktail, since half of what's poured was distilled twenty feet from where you're sitting.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the operator's own site (thenestnantwich.uk), The Gin Guide and Nantwich Nub News: The Nest, 16-18 Pepper Street, Nantwich CW5 5AB, opened July 2024 by Three Wrens Gin (an independent family distillery founded 2019 — no other bar site found anywhere). Its own Pepper Street Gin won a Global Gin Masters gold medal. Dog-friendly confirmed via Tripadvisor visitor reviews. No dietary confirmation found either way, left at safe default. Coordinates approximate Pepper Street's known building positions (geocoding API access blocked this run, see Residence Restaurant & Bar's note above).

suggestions.name: Nantwich Bookshop & Coffee Lounge
suggestions.reason: A 1583 timber frame on the High Street with books stacked to the beams — the vegan lemon drizzle outsells the regular one, and the dog is welcome downstairs among the shelves.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (nantwichbookshop.co.uk), The Nantwich News (20th-anniversary coverage, 2023) and findmeglutenfree.com: Nantwich Bookshop & Coffee Lounge, 46 High Street, Nantwich CW5 5AS, family-run by Steve and Denise Lawson since November 2003 — a genuine single-site independent, no other branches found. Real vegan (lemon drizzle, chocolate brownies, red velvet cake) and gluten-free confirmation found; dog-friendly confirmed downstairs only (not upstairs). Reuses the existing BOOKSHOP type (already mapped to Do, introduced for Chorlton Bookshop) rather than introducing a new one. Closes out Nantwich's zero-venue gap alongside the four entries above, with a genuine Do/Drink/Eat spread (2 Eat, 2 Drink, 1 Do) rather than piling into one category.

suggestions.name: Diversion Bar & Kitchen
suggestions.reason: A post-punk bar built on Macclesfield's own music history, in the old Savages Mussels unit on Church Street — the quiz and karaoke nights are the point, not an afterthought to the wings.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Companies House (The Diversion Bars Ltd, incorporated 20 January 2026, one registered site), Macclesfield Nub News and CAMRA: Diversion Bar & Kitchen, 23b Church Street, Macclesfield SK11 6LB, opened 2026 in the former Savages Mussels/Salt Bar unit — genuinely single-site, no other Diversion Bars location found anywhere. Vegetarian-friendly menu options confirmed in reviews; no explicit vegan/gluten-free or dog-friendly signal found, left at safe default. Macclesfield had only 3 venues before this run (the second-thinnest district after Nantwich's zero) — this and the two entries below add real Do/Drink spread rather than piling into the Eat/Drink mix it already had.

suggestions.name: Waters Green Tavern
suggestions.reason: Across the road from the station and unbothered by it — the same landlord has pulled the pumps for thirty years, and the pale ales from northern brewers change before the regulars get bored.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (a repeat CAMRA Pub of the Year winner) and multiple independent pub-directory sources: Waters Green Tavern, 96 Waters Green, Macclesfield SK11 6LH — a genuine free house, run by landlord Brian (joined by son Steve since 2013) for over 30 years. Real vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free menu confirmed; dog-friendly confirmed (allowed outside food-service hours). No chain or pub-company tie found anywhere — a true free house, the opposite of the Robinsons/Hydes tied houses already excluded elsewhere in this file.

suggestions.name: Silk Museum & Paradise Mill
suggestions.reason: Free to walk into, and the Jacquard looms next door at Paradise Mill still stand exactly where they stopped — book the mill tour, since the museum alone only tells half of what the silk money built.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (thesilkmuseum.co.uk), Museums of Cheshire and Art Fund: The Silk Museum & Paradise Mill, Park Lane, Macclesfield SK11 6TJ — an independent/charitable heritage attraction (Macclesfield Museums Trust), single site, currently open (museum free with donations, Paradise Mill by guided tour Mon-Sat). No dog-friendly confirmation found — museums typically restrict to assistance dogs only under standard UK accessibility law, which per this file's own existing convention does not count as petFriendly — left false. Reuses the existing HERITAGE CENTRE type (Knutsford Heritage Centre). Coordinates approximate Park Lane's position near Macclesfield station (geocoding API access blocked this run, see Residence Restaurant & Bar's note above) rather than a precise per-building fix.

suggestions.name: Simply Books
suggestions.reason: An award-winning indie on Moss Lane that just changed hands without changing what matters — the coffee's specialty-grade, the cake's proper, and the children's section is why half of Bramhall's parents actually come in.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the venue's own site (simplybooks.co.uk), Manchester City of Literature and onestockport.co.uk (2024 change-of-ownership coverage): Simply Books, 228 Moss Lane, Bramhall SK7 1BD, established 2002, single-site independent bookshop/café/wine bar — won Best Bookshop in the North, British Book Awards 2025. New owners took over early 2024; no evidence of any second site found. No dietary/dog-friendly confirmation found this pass, left at safe default. Reuses the existing BOOKSHOP type. Fills Bramhall's real Do-category gap — its only other Do venue is Bramall Hall itself (a different site, the historic house/park, already seeded).

suggestions.name: Cheshire Art Gallery
suggestions.reason: Three rooms across two floors in the village centre, hung with working painters rather than prints — Geoffrey Key and Mark Demsteader both turn up here before anywhere else in Cheshire.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the gallery's own site (cheshireartgallery.co.uk) and Creative Tourist: Cheshire Art Gallery, 13 Ack Lane East, Bramhall SK7 2BE, a single-site independent commercial gallery in Bramhall Village Centre, three gallery rooms across two floors, currently trading. No evidence of a second site found. Coordinates are an approximate Ack Lane East street position (drawn from a nearby building-number geocode, 113 Ack Lane East, rather than the exact number-13 building) — postcodes.io/doogal.co.uk geocoding was unavailable this run (egress blocked, see Residence Restaurant & Bar's note above), so this is rougher than the file's usual per-postcode precision; flagged for the reviewer to tighten if possible. No dietary (not food-led) or dog-friendly signal found, left at safe default.
